title: Grid Model: An Entropic and Dynamic Theory for Emergent Gravity in Cosmology
description: Proposes an Energy-Flow Cosmology (EFC) Grid Model in which gravity emerges from entropy-regulated energy flow rather than from dark matter or a cosmological constant. The paper links entropy, energy-flow gradients, and a dynamic effective gravity to observed rotation curves, gravitational lensing trends, high-ℓ CMB anisotropy deviations, and environment-dependent gravitational-wave propagation, supported by simulations and comparisons to JWST, SDSS/eFEDS, Planck, HST, and LIGO data.

entropy_energy_flow_relation.description: Linear increases in entropy correspond to an exponential decrease in energy flow, stabilizing or collapsing spacetime at the entropy extrema.

emergent_speed_of_light.description: The effective speed of light emerges from energy-flow gradients, remains approximately constant at intermediate entropy, and diminishes toward zero near entropy extremes.

effective_gravity_scaling.description: Gravity is dynamically weakened in higher-entropy environments via an entropy-dependent effective gravitational coupling.

cmb_damping_factor.description: A thermodynamic damping factor modifies high-ℓ CMB anisotropies, predicting an O(7%) deviation relative to ΛCDM at multipoles above ~1000.

key_results.main_finding: An entropy-regulated energy-flow framework reproduces galaxy rotation trends, predicts an anti-correlation of lensing strength with entropy, allows ~7% high-ℓ CMB deviations, and remains consistent with current gravitational-wave speed limits via environmental dependence, without invoking dark matter or Λ.
parameters_tested: Halo regulator model for energy-flow stabilization

sealed_predictions.statement: CMB temperature/polarization power spectra exhibit a ≈7% suppression at ℓ > 1000 relative to ΛCDM due to a thermodynamic damping factor γ(S).
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: High-precision ACT/SPT-3G/Simons Observatory + Planck spectra showing no such suppression beyond systematic/modeling uncertainties.

sealed_predictions.statement: Gravitational lensing convergence and shear statistically anti-correlate with independent entropy proxies; lensing is amplified in low-entropy clusters and diminished in high-entropy voids.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Weak-lensing tomography cross-correlated with X-ray/SZ entropy maps and IGM thermodynamic tracers failing to show a robust anti-correlation.

sealed_predictions.statement: Environment-dependent deviations in gravitational-wave propagation speed are negligible in low-entropy regions but measurably larger in high-entropy environments (e.g., massive clusters, BH mergers), while remaining consistent with existing neutron-star constraints.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Multimessenger GW-EM timing across environments consistently yielding |Δc_g/c| < 10^-15 with no entropy dependence.

sealed_predictions.statement: Galaxy rotation curves can be fit without cold dark matter using G_eff(S) governed by halo-regulated energy flow.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: A representative sample of high-quality HI/optical rotation curves and vertical dispersions that cannot be fit under any plausible α and g(S) within the model.

kill_criteria: KC1: High-ℓ (ℓ > 1000) CMB measurements (ACT/SPT/Simons/Planck) show no ≈7% deviation or show a deviation with opposite sign after foreground/systematic control.
KC2: Multimessenger GW-EM observations in high-entropy environments (e.g., cluster-hosted BH mergers) constrain |Δc_g/c| below 10^-16 with no measurable dependence on entropy proxies.
KC3: Weak-lensing maps fail to show an anti-correlation between lensing strength and independent entropy indicators (X-ray/SZ/IGM), or show a positive correlation inconsistent with model predictions.
KC4: Galaxy rotation curves across low-entropy systems require substantial cold dark matter to fit, with no consistent G_eff(S) solution across the sample.

KC5: Bullet Cluster–like mergers robustly require collisionless dark matter to explain mass–gas separation and lensing maps, with the proposed entropic interaction term unable to reproduce observations.
KC6: Precision tests find G_eff to be invariant with environmental entropy across scales where the model predicts variation.
KC7: Observational evidence shows gravitational lensing does not diminish in high-entropy voids relative to comparable-mass lower-entropy environments.
